overview.title: What is Network School?
overview.text: Network School is a residential startup society in Forest City, Malaysia, where founders, engineers, and builders live and work together near Singapore.

overview.title: Who joins Network School?
overview.text: Members come from 80+ countries and work across crypto, AI, biotech, media, and startup-society research. The community skews toward founders, engineers, writers, athletes, and coaches who are building alternatives to legacy institutions. Families with children are explicitly welcome, and the age range spans toddlers to experienced operators.

overview.title: What does Network School teach?
overview.text: The curriculum covers the rise and fall of states, startup societies, and civilizations - from the Meiji Restoration to Singapore's founding, from the collapse of Argentina to the growth of crypto. Practical tracks include AI and blockchain hackathons, guest lectures from founders and investors, and a credentialing program that issues verifiable on-chain certificates. Monthly themes organize programming around focused areas: past months have covered Ethereum and AI.

history.text:
Network School was founded by [Balaji Srinivasan](https://balajis.com/p/network-school) and launched in August 2024 with the acquisition of a campus at Forest City, a largely vacant island development in Malaysia near Singapore. Balaji announced the campus - secured through cryptocurrency - as a place for builders to live together and work on the next generation of startup societies.

The V1 cohort ran from September 23 to December 23, 2024 - a 90-day proof of concept that received 4,000+ applications and enrolled 128 participants from 80+ countries. Notable guest speakers included Vitalik Buterin, Bryan Johnson, Brian Armstrong, and Garry Tan. The main lesson from V1: the cohort model attracted too many people with short time horizons.

V2 launched on March 1, 2025 as a year-long program with doubled capacity (256 members) and a greater focus on long-term builders. The all-inclusive fee structure - covering accommodation, three meals a day, gym, coworking, and all programming - replaced the V1 model where food was billed separately.

V3, a permanent campus nearby that would house 1,024 or more residents, was in active development as of early 2026.

location:
Network School is situated at Forest City, a manmade island in Johor, Malaysia, within the Singapore-Johor Special Economic Zone (SEZ). The campus occupies buildings in a Country Garden development originally constructed as part of China's Belt and Road Initiative; most on-site retail signage is in Chinese, though the NS community itself is internationally mixed.

Forest City sits roughly 1 hour by car from central Singapore. NS provides shuttle service for residents, and the SEZ is designed to ease cross-border movement for skilled workers. The location puts 50%+ of the global population within a short flight, which Balaji cites as a core reason for choosing this site over Western hubs.
duration: Network School (V2) operates as a year-long program. New members may join on the 1st of each month, and shorter stays of around one month are possible. Long-term residents committing to a full year are housed in refurbished apartments in a building directly adjacent to the main hotel; shorter-stay participants stay in fully furnished hotel rooms. The campus typically holds 80-120 people at any given time.
pricing:
Shared or double room: $1,500/month
Private room: $3,000/month

Both tiers are all-inclusive - the fee covers accommodation, three meals per day (following the Blueprint longevity protocol developed with Bryan Johnson), gym access with personal trainers, coworking space, high-speed internet, and all workshops, hackathons, and courses. Cryptocurrency payment is accepted.

Applying through the [wagmit referral link](https://ns.com/wagmit/apply) gives new members one week free.
amenities: Furnished accommodation (hotel room for short-term; apartment for 1-year residents)
Three meals per day following the Blueprint longevity diet
Access to all workshops, hackathons, and courses
Guest lectures from founders, investors, and researchers
AI and blockchain credentialing program (on-chain certificates)
Monthly themed programming (e.g., AI Month, ETH Month)
Shuttle service to and from Singapore
fellowship:
The Network School Fellowship funds 100 fellows per cohort with $100,000 each. Fellows must relocate to the NS campus for one year. The program targets tech founders (particularly those building for Asian markets), AI-first creators, community builders, and what Balaji calls 'dark talent' - undiscovered people from underrepresented regions globally.

Funding covers early-stage ventures at competitive seed valuations, or negotiated terms for companies that already have investors. Since monthly campus costs run around $1,500 all-inclusive, a $100K check effectively provides more than five years of personal runway while living and building on campus.

The four-stage selection process: an online form with a screening test and references, a structured video interview assessing integrity and agency, an in-person proctored written exam at the campus (comparable in rigor to the SAT or IIT JEE), and finally relocation. English fluency is required; any country of origin is accepted.
longtermer: Long-term members committing to a full year are housed in refurbished apartments in a dedicated building directly in front of the main hotel, rather than in hotel rooms. V2 was designed with long-term builders as the primary target - the stated top criterion for admission is finding people who want to build alongside the NS community over the long run. Long-term residents participate in all NS programming, events, and credentialing while enjoying apartment-style private living separate from the hotel floors.

kidFriendly.description: Network School explicitly welcomes families and children. Kids can attend formal Malaysian schooling while their parents participate in NS programming. The community is intergenerational - personal trainers interact with kids, founders teach coding to children, and residents describe their children gaining '50 aunties and uncles from 30 countries.' Organized activities for babies, toddlers, and older kids run regularly on campus. Detailed family-specific information is available at [ns.com/wiki](https://ns.com/wiki).

discount.text: Apply through the wagmit referral link and get your first week at Network School free. This is the canonical referral link maintained by the NS team.

howToEnter.text: Apply online at [ns.com/wagmit/apply](https://ns.com/wagmit/apply) (using this referral link gives one week free). The standard application includes an online form with a screening test and references, followed by a structured video interview. Fellowship applicants go through two additional rounds: an in-person proctored exam at the campus and final selection. New members join on the 1st of each month.

faqs.question: Where is Network School located?
faqs.answer: Network School is at Forest City, a manmade island in Johor, Malaysia, within the Singapore-Johor Special Economic Zone. It is roughly 1 hour by car from central Singapore, with shuttle service available for residents.

faqs.question: How much does Network School cost?
faqs.answer: A shared or double room costs $1,500/month all-inclusive. A private room costs $3,000/month all-inclusive. Both cover accommodation, three meals per day, gym, personal trainers, coworking, internet, and all programming. Applying through the [wagmit link](https://ns.com/wagmit/apply) gives one week free.

faqs.question: What is included in the Network School membership fee?
faqs.answer: The monthly fee covers accommodation, three meals per day (following the Blueprint longevity protocol), gym access with personal trainers, coworking space, high-speed internet, all workshops and hackathons, guest lectures, and access to the credentialing program. There are no additional fees for on-campus programming.

faqs.question: Who should apply to Network School?
faqs.answer: Network School is designed for founders, engineers, AI builders, crypto developers, writers, athletes, coaches, and anyone building in tech or startup-society research. The community values openness, decentralization, and classical-liberal or centrist politics. Families are welcome, and the age range on campus spans toddlers to experienced operators.

faqs.question: How long do people stay at Network School?
faqs.answer: V2 is designed as a year-long program, though members can join on the 1st of each month and shorter stays of around one month are possible. Long-term residents committing to a full year are housed in apartments; shorter-stay members are in hotel rooms.

faqs.question: Can I bring my family or children to Network School?
faqs.answer: Yes. NS explicitly welcomes families. Children can attend formal Malaysian schooling while living on campus. The community is intergenerational, with regular organized activities for babies, toddlers, and older kids. See [ns.com/wiki](https://ns.com/wiki) for family-specific details.

faqs.question: What is the Network School Fellowship?
faqs.answer: The Fellowship funds 100 members with $100,000 each to spend one year building on campus. It targets tech founders, AI-first creators, and talented people from underrepresented backgrounds. Selection involves an online form, video interview, in-person proctored exam, and relocation. [Learn more and apply at ns.com/fellowship](https://ns.com/fellowship).

faqs.question: Who has spoken at Network School?
faqs.answer: Past speakers include Vitalik Buterin, Bryan Johnson, Brian Armstrong (Coinbase), Garry Tan (Y Combinator), Naval Ravikant, Niall Ferguson, Glenn Greenwald, Ryan Petersen (Flexport), Pieter Levels, Amjad Masad (Replit), Codie Sanchez, Olaf Carlson-Wee, Haseeb Qureshi, and Ayaan Hirsi Ali, among others.

faqs.question: How many people are at Network School at once?
faqs.answer: V2 has a total capacity of 256 members, with roughly 80-120 people on campus at any given time. The original V1 cohort (2024) had 128 participants from 80+ countries and received 4,000+ applications.

faqs.question: What events and programming does Network School run?
faqs.answer: NS holds 2-3 all-hands sessions per week and a full community-driven events calendar. Monthly themes organize programming around topics like AI and Ethereum. Past activities include lecture series, hackathons, comedy improv, morning pages, language classes, and community dinners. The live events calendar is at [luma.com/ns](https://luma.com/ns).

faqs.question: What changed between V1 and V2 of Network School?
faqs.answer: V1 (Sept-Dec 2024) was a 90-day cohort for 128 members where food was billed separately. V2 (from March 2025) is a year-long program for 256 members with an all-inclusive fee covering food, gym, coworking, and all programming. V2 focuses on long-term builders rather than short-stay participants.

faqs.question: Can I pay for Network School with cryptocurrency?
faqs.answer: Yes, cryptocurrency payment is accepted for the monthly membership fee.
